# 1 Samuel Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 133r–133v | **Source Image:** 1SA_003_page_001.jpg, 1SA_003_page_002.jpg

---

**1** The boy Samuel served the LORD under Eli's supervision. In those days, messages from the LORD were rare — visions were uncommon.

**2** One night Eli was lying down in his usual place. His eyesight had grown so weak that he could barely see.

**3** The lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying down in the LORD's temple, near the ark of God.

**4** Then the LORD called out, "Samuel!" And Samuel answered, "Here I am!"

**5** He ran to Eli and said, "Here I am — you called me." But Eli said, "I didn't call you. Go back and lie down." So he went back and lay down.

**6** The LORD called again, "Samuel!" Samuel got up, went to Eli, and said, "Here I am — you called me." Eli replied, "I didn't call you, my son. Go back and lie down."

**7** Samuel had not yet come to know the LORD personally, and the LORD had not yet spoken directly to him.

**8** The LORD called Samuel a third time. He got up, went to Eli, and said, "Here I am — you called me." Then Eli realized that it was the LORD calling the boy.

**9** So Eli told Samuel, "Go and lie down, and if He calls you again, say, 'Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.'" Samuel went back and lay down in his place.

**10** Then the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, "Samuel! Samuel!" And Samuel said, "Speak, for Your servant is listening."

**11** The LORD said to Samuel, "I am about to do something in Israel that will make the ears of everyone who hears about it ring.

**12** On that day I will carry out against Eli everything I have spoken against his family — every word, from beginning to end.

**13** I told him that I would judge his family forever because of the sin he knew about: his sons were blaspheming God, and he failed to restrain them.

**14** Therefore I have sworn to Eli's family: the guilt of his house will never be wiped away by sacrifice or offering — ever."

**15** Samuel lay there until morning, then got up and opened the doors of the LORD's house. He was afraid to tell Eli about the vision.

**16** But Eli called to him, "Samuel, my son!" He answered, "Here I am."

**17** "What did He say to you?" Eli asked. "Don't hide it from me. May God deal with you severely if you hide a single word of everything He told you."

**18** So Samuel told him everything, holding nothing back. And Eli said, "He is the LORD. Let Him do what He sees as right."

**19** As Samuel grew up, the LORD was with him, and He confirmed every word Samuel spoke.

**20** All Israel, from Dan in the north to Beer-sheba in the south, recognized that Samuel had been established as a prophet of the LORD.

**21** And the LORD continued to appear at Shiloh, because it was there that the LORD revealed Himself to Samuel through His word.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **3:1 — "rare" and "uncommon"**: The Hebrew יָקָר means "precious/rare" and נִפְרָץ means "breaking forth." I have translated the combined sense: God's direct communication was both infrequent and not spreading widely. This sets up the dramatic significance of what follows — God breaking His silence.

2. **3:3 — "the lamp of God"**: This is both a literal time-marker (the temple lamp burned from evening to morning) and a metaphor. The old priesthood's light is nearly extinguished, but God is about to kindle a new flame through Samuel.

3. **3:7 — "had not yet come to know the LORD personally"**: The Hebrew ידע ("know") here means experiential, direct knowledge through prophetic revelation — not intellectual belief. Samuel knew about God; he had not yet heard from God.

4. **3:10 — "came and stood there"**: The Hebrew conveys that the LORD physically stationed Himself — this is a theophany, a divine appearance, not just a voice in the dark. The double call "Samuel! Samuel!" echoes the calls to Abraham and Moses.

5. **3:13 — "blaspheming God"**: The Masoretic tradition notes this as a possible scribal correction (tiqqun sopherim). The original may have read "cursing God" directly, softened to "bringing a curse on themselves." PNEUMA renders the force of the original.

6. **3:18 — "He is the LORD"**: Eli's three-word response is one of the most poignant moments in the book — total submission to a devastating divine verdict against his own family. No protest, no bargaining. Just acceptance.

— PNEUMA
